notifications.title: Push notifications
notifications.intro: Get notified on your phone the moment a new photo, comment, or entry is added. Turn on and test notifications for this device below.

thisDevice.title: This device
thisDevice.hint: After turning notifications on, tap Send test notification to get a sample on this device. If it doesn't arrive, check the platform guides below.

android.title: Android app
android.step1: Install the bebe app, enter your server address, and sign in.
android.step2: Turn on Receive notifications on this device above, then Allow the Android notification permission.
android.step3: Tap Send test notification to confirm it arrives.
android.note: App push only works once an admin sets up Firebase (FCM). If the permission prompt didn't appear or was declined, you can enable it in your phone's Settings → Apps → bebe → Notifications.

web.title: Web browser
web.step1: Open the site in Chrome, Edge, etc. and turn on Receive notifications on this device above.
web.note: If you blocked it by mistake, change it via the lock icon → Notifications → Allow on the left of the address bar, then turn it on again. Installing to your home screen (PWA) makes delivery more reliable.

ios.title: iPhone · iPad
ios.step1: Open the site in Safari, tap the share button → Add to Home Screen.
ios.step2: Reopen the site from the bebe icon now on your home screen.
ios.step3: Turn on Receive notifications on this device above, allow the permission, then test.
ios.note: On iPhone, push only works when added to the home screen. You can't enable it from a Safari tab (Apple policy).

categories.title: Choose which alerts to receive
categories.hint: Turn the alert types you want on or off below. (This applies to your whole account, not per device.)

admin.title: Admin settings
admin.hint: For notifications to reach the whole family, an admin needs to turn them on once:
admin.step2: Generate the VAPID keys for web push (one button).
admin.step3: Enter the Firebase service account + client config for app push.
admin.step4: Turn on the alert categories you want delivered.

backup.title: Backup / Restore
backup.subtitle: Back up photos & settings
backup.createDesc: Bundles your DB (settings & metadata) plus photos and videos into one file in the backup folder. Full includes every photo; incremental only includes new photos since the last backup.
backup.creating: Creating backup… (this can take a while with many photos)
backup.autoDesc: Backs up automatically at a set time. Every {every}th run is full, the rest are incremental.
backup.includeSecretDesc: Needed to restore encrypted settings (OIDC, push, sessions). Not included by default.
backup.secretWarn: Caution — this backup file is like a password vault. If SECRET_KEY is included, this single file unlocks all of your OIDC, push, and session secrets. Never share it externally, and keep it only in trusted storage.
backup.remoteDesc: After creating a backup, also upload it to an S3-compatible store (B2, MinIO, S3, etc.).
backup.endpointPlaceholder: Endpoint (e.g. https://s3.us-west-002.backblazeb2.com; leave empty for AWS)
backup.secretKeySavedPlaceholder: Secret Access Key (saved — enter only to change)
backup.saveToApplyHint: Press Save to apply. The secret key is stored encrypted and won't be shown again.
backup.restoreSecretWarn: ⚠️ If this backup was made with a different SECRET_KEY, encrypted settings won't decrypt after restore (use CLI restore in that case).
backup.restoreMismatch: Input didn't match, so it was cancelled.
backup.restoring: Restoring… the app will restart automatically when done.
backup.restoreDone: Restore complete — the app is restarting. We'll refresh automatically…
backup.restoreTimeout: Restore finished. If the app doesn't come back, refresh manually.
backup.howToWeb: Restore from the web: use the ↺ button in the list above → enter the backup id → restore. When done, the app restarts automatically (for same-instance rollback).
backup.howToDisaster: Full / disaster recovery (new device or different SECRET_KEY): place the backup file in the backup folder, then on the server run:

auth.title: Auth settings
auth.publicSignupHint: Only the first user (admin) can sign up publicly to create the family. After that, new members join by invite link only.
auth.name: Name
auth.kakaoScopeHint: Kakao requires business-app review for the email consent item — drop account_email to sign up with nickname only.
auth.clientSecretEncryptedHint: Stored in the DB encrypted with AES-256-GCM using SECRET_KEY.
auth.redirectUriHint: Register this value in your provider console's Redirect URIs.
auth.redirectUriNote: Register this Redirect URI in the provider console as-is. It stays the same after saving.
auth.guidePlaceholder: Choose a provider to see a step-by-step guide here.
auth.securityClaims: iss · aud · exp · nonce · state verification
auth.securityEncryption: Client Secret stored with AES-256-GCM encryption
auth.googleStep1Body: Console → Credentials → "Create credentials" → "OAuth client ID" → choose application type "Web application".
auth.googleStep2Body:
Copy the URI below and paste it into "Authorized redirect URIs" in the Google console:
{uri}
auth.googleStep3Body: Copy the client ID and password shown after saving, paste them into the form below, and save.
auth.googleStep4Body: Google sets email_verified=true by default. If an account with the same email already exists, it links automatically.
auth.kakaoStep1Body: Kakao Developers → My Applications → Add an application. Note the REST API key after saving.
auth.kakaoStep2Body: App settings → Platform → Web → register your current service URL as the site domain.
auth.kakaoStep3Body:
Product → Kakao Login → turn ON, and on the same screen **also turn ON OpenID Connect** (both must be on). Register the value below as the Redirect URI:
{uri}
auth.kakaoStep4Body: In consent items, set Nickname (profile_nickname) to ON. Email (account_email) requires business-app review, so it's excluded by default — Kakao can sign up with nickname only (no email).
auth.kakaoStep5Body: Security → generate Client Secret code → set to ON → copy the code. Paste it into Client Secret in the form below.
auth.kakaoStep6Body: App keys → paste the REST API key value into Client ID in the form below.
auth.naverStep1Body: Naver Developers → Register application → choose "Naver Login" as the API in use.
auth.naverStep2Body: Set member name and email address to "Required". Without email, account linking is limited.
auth.naverStep3Body:
Set your current service address as the Service URL, and register the value below as the Callback URL:
{uri}
auth.naverStep4Body: Paste the issued Client ID and Client Secret into the form below. (Naver uses OAuth2, so no Issuer is needed.)
auth.microsoftStep1Body: Azure Portal → App Registrations → New Registration. Choose supported account types.
auth.microsoftStep2Body:
Platform: Web. Enter the value below as the URI:
{uri}
auth.microsoftStep3Body: Certificates & secrets → New client secret → copy the Value (you can't see it again once the window closes).
auth.microsoftStep4Body: Copy the "Application (client) ID" from the Overview screen.
auth.microsoftStep5Body: The default tenant may not include an email claim. Token configuration → Optional claims → ID → adding email is recommended.
auth.microsoftStep6Body: To allow only a single tenant, change the Issuer to https://login.microsoftonline.com/<TENANT-ID>/v2.0.
auth.customStep1Body: Any OIDC-compliant IdP (Keycloak, Authelia, Authentik, Dex, etc.) can connect. The issuer is usually in the form <IdP-URL>/realms/<realm>.
auth.customStep2Body:
Register the value below in your IdP console's Allowed Redirect URIs:
{uri}
auth.customStep3Body: The id_token must include sub, email, email_verified, and name.

firebaseGuide.summary: How to set up Firebase (one-time, step by step)
firebaseGuide.intro: To send push to the Android app you need a free Firebase project. Grab the two items below (a server service account + the app config) from the console and paste them on this page.
firebaseGuide.g1s1: In the Firebase console, click Add project. Name it anything (e.g. bebe).
firebaseGuide.g1s2: You can skip Google Analytics. Click Create project to finish.
firebaseGuide.group2Title: 2. For the server — service account key (secret)
firebaseGuide.g2s1: Go to the gear ⚙️ at the top left → Project settings → Service accounts tab.
firebaseGuide.g2s2: Click Generate new private key → Generate key to download a JSON file.
firebaseGuide.g2s3: Open that JSON file, copy the whole thing, paste it into the Service account JSON field above, and Save.
firebaseGuide.g2s4: In the Cloud Messaging tab, confirm Firebase Cloud Messaging API (V1) is enabled (usually on by default).
firebaseGuide.secretWarning: ⚠️ The service account JSON is a secret, like a password. Don't share it over chat or email — paste it only here (it's stored encrypted on the server).
firebaseGuide.group3Title: 3. For the app — Firebase config values (public)
firebaseGuide.g3s1: Project settings → General tab → under Your apps, click the Android icon to add an app.
firebaseGuide.g3s2: For Android package name, enter exactly (nickname is free, SHA-1 can be blank) → Register app.
firebaseGuide.g3s3: Download the google-services.json file. Open it in a text editor and you'll find these four values:
firebaseGuide.g3s4: Paste the four values into the App Firebase config field above in this shape and Save:
firebaseGuide.g4s1: On this page, turn on the Android app push (FCM) toggle and the notification master at the top.
firebaseGuide.g4s2: Family members turn on notifications in the app under Settings → Notifications → Push notifications and confirm with Send test notification.
